findings.summary: Equal-start part precedence is special-cased only on the start page.
findings.consequence: For two parts with the same start page, the Reader can report the first source-ordered part on the shared start page, then switch to the later source-ordered part on following overlapping pages without a new part boundary. This may be intended for overlap depth, but it differs from a stable source-order tie rule.
findings.evidence: Line 27 gives `starting` precedence over `active.at(-1)`, so exact start pages choose the first sorted equal-start part. On later pages within both equal-start ranges, `starting` is undefined and `active.at(-1)` chooses the last equal-start source. The named tests assert first same-start selection at the start page but do not cover the following overlapping page.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the desired equal-start rule. If source order should win for the whole overlapping span, derive `currentPartIndex` from the first active equal-start group consistently; if deepest/latest active span should win, remove the `starting` exception and update tests to encode that rule.
